most_likely_actual_diagnosis_free_text: Invasive group A streptococcal infection with streptococcal toxic shock syndrome: necrotizing soft-tissue infection of the left chest/abdominal wall, left-sided pneumonia with effusions, and bacteremia, possibly after a viral respiratory infection
one_line_reason: She had contact with someone who had a respiratory infection, then developed a fulminant febrile illness with GI prodrome, early shock, multi-organ failure (AKI, raised CK, low platelets, coagulopathy, hypoxemia), leukopenia, very high CRP and PCT, and a rapidly spreading phlegmon with bullae plus a large left lung infiltrate. This pattern is classic for streptococcal toxic shock from invasive S. pyogenes.
